Ramses is the name of the Pharaoh we made our Exodus from. Some scholars say nobody knows which Pharaoh it was. No, the Bible tells you.

points: Miriam was crafty. She offered to call a nurse of the Hebrew women, and Pharaoh's daughter sent the maid, who called the child's own mother, and wages were paid her to nurse him.
The child grew, and he became the son of Pharaoh's daughter. She called his name Moses, which means drawn out, because she drew him out of the water.
When Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses; but Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian.

Moses gave up his whole upbringing and position. By faith he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. In Egypt his head was shaved, his beard cut, his dress and customs Egyptian; he laid all of it down to be what he was called to be, an Israelite.

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God. Understand: in ancient Egypt, everybody was not bad off. Things were not bad for Moses; Moses made things bad for himself by killing the Egyptian.

points: You know what kind of honor it was to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter? You had wealth, fame, everything; Moses gave it all up.

By faith and suffering through Christ: that’s the same thing our forefather Moses did. He rather suffer affliction with his people. “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter”: he refused to follow their customs.
